close_reason: Opinion-ratified: closure shape kept workspace-wide per the bead's own recommendation. No code change. Workspace-lints-table plumbing for a forward-looking workspace-level allow is out of scope for a P3 opinion bead.
description:
Sites: clippy::redundant_closure_for_method_calls fires 45 times in chat-server src/, 26 times in mail-server src/ (canonical sibling). Total ~70+ workspace-wide.

Representative patterns:

(a) .map(|id| id.as_ref())               → .map(AsRef::as_ref)
(b) .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())            → .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool)
(c) .into_iter().map(|s| s.into()).collect() → .into_iter().map(Into::into).collect()
(d) result.iter().map(|id| id.as_ref()).collect() → result.iter().map(AsRef::as_ref).collect()

Why opinion-labeled: the clippy default suggests the function-pointer shape, but for a Rust reader the closure shape is often MORE readable than the method-reference shape, especially for (a) and (d). Compare:

    result.removed.iter().map(|id| id.as_ref()).collect()   // closure
    result.removed.iter().map(AsRef::as_ref).collect()       // method ref

The closure-shape reads as 'for each id, call .as_ref()'. The method-ref shape reads as 'apply this function to each element', but the reader has to mentally resolve 'which AsRef::as_ref does this dispatch to, given the element type?'. For the chat handler context where id is always &Id (and the AsRef impl is unambiguous), both shapes compile to the same thing, but the closure is what a senior Rust reviewer would actually write — closure-fn-equivalence is not 'cleaner', it's just 'shorter'.

The (b) shape (.and_then(|v| v.as_bool())) is slightly stronger for the method-ref rewrite because the chain is longer (and_then takes a fn pointer naturally), but it still doesn't pass the 'a serious Rust practitioner would wince' bar.

What goes wrong if left: nothing functionally. clippy::pedantic is opt-in and the warnings are not enabled by default. Filed only to capture that this lint family was reviewed and intentionally not applied workspace-wide.

If the workspace decides to apply (preferred direction would be 'no, leave the closures'), file the decision as a workspace-level lint allow:

    # at workspace root or via cfg_attr
    #![allow(clippy::redundant_closure_for_method_calls)]

so future contributors don't have to re-decide. That would be the cleanest closure of this finding.

clippy::pedantic verified 2026-05-16 against current HEAD. Opinion-labeled because the engineering basis for either direction is weak.
title: Workspace-canonical: redundant_closure_for_method_calls — 45 sites in chat-server + 26 in mail-server
